requirement:
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.

When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
rationale:
I found no gap. Every obligation maps to reachable code and has a test that runs it and asserts the outcome.

**Obligations**
1. Every definition referenced by the subject or any contributed source contributes its complete fenced declaration, including the phrase option.
2. Definitions referenced by those definitions are included transitively.
3. The transitive set has no duplicates.
4. The transitive set does not fail to terminate on cycles.
5. When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same complete, transitive set is supplied to the model before a submission is accepted.
6. That same set is recorded before a submission is accepted.

**Code**
- **Initial inputs, obligations 1–4.** `src/authoring/inputs.rs#impl[AssessmentSources]/fn[prepare]` carries the `{impl}` reference. It builds the mandatory selectors, then calls `definition_inputs(…, &mandatory, Some(&subject.text))`.
  - `src/authoring/inputs.rs#fn[definition_inputs]` calls `crate::terms::dependencies`.
  - `src/terms.rs#fn[direct_references]` collects `{term}` references from the subject text and from every contributed input. It scans comments in outline sources, declaration bodies in requirement inputs, and definition inputs directly.
  - `src/terms.rs#fn[close_dependencies]` expands to a fixed point using a `visited` set and a `BTreeSet`. This gives transitivity, no duplicates, and termination on cycles.
  - Each name then goes through `source_input`, which resolves `InputSelector::Definition` in `src/inputs.rs#impl[InputSelector]/fn[resolve]`. The text is `redact_lines(&target.raw_lines)`. The `raw_lines` are the full fenced declaration, which includes the `:phrase:` line. The tests assert this.
- **Later reads, obligations 5–6.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#fn[converse]` carries the `{impl}` reference. It calls `tools::dispatch_paged`.
  - `read` in `src/authoring/tools.rs` and `ResultPages::deliver` in `src/authoring/pages.rs` call `additional_definitions` and `definitions_each`. These run the same `definition_inputs` and drop only definitions already delivered or recorded.
  - The definitions are added to the tool result, so the model receives them.
  - They are also added to `pending`.
  - `converse` calls `sources.record_inputs(&pending)` on the next response, before it evaluates and accepts a submission.

**Tests**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[bundle_combines_direct_references_terms_and_current_existing_selectors]` has two definitions that reference each other, `unit` and `value`. It asserts exactly two definition inputs. That covers transitivity, deduplication and the cycle.
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[mandatory_git_inputs_require_staging_declarations_sources_and_terms]` asserts that a referenced term is supplied as a definition input.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[definitions_introduced_by_a_read_are_supplied_and_recorded_before_submission]` has a cyclic `unit`/`value` pair introduced by a read. It asserts these things:
  - The recorded evidence lists `terms.unit` and `terms.value` once each.
  - Each recorded definition's text begins with `:::{definition}` and `:phrase:`.
  - The second request, the one that precedes the submission, contains the definition text.
  - The first request does not contain it.
- `src/authoring/pages.rs#mod[tests]/fn[paged_inputs_carry_their_definitions_and_deliver_only_their_own_inputs]` and `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` cover the paged and line-range read paths. They assert that the definitions travel with the delivered inputs and are recorded once.

All of these tests carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. I found no unspecified behavior and no `{fixme}` reference to the subject.

text: :::{req} authoring_inputs
When preparing the mandatory input set defined by
{cite}`requirements.authoring.mandatory_inputs`, every terminology definition
referenced by the subject or any contributed source MUST contribute its complete
fenced declaration, including its phrase option. Definitions referenced by those
definitions MUST also be included transitively, without duplicates or
nontermination on cycles.
When an additional source read introduces a terminology dependency, the same
complete, transitive definition set MUST be supplied to the model and recorded
before accepting a submission.
:::{req} mandatory_inputs
The harness MUST construct each assessment's mandatory input set by combining
the contributions specified by the requirements applicable to that subject and
its inputs. A requirement that contributes inputs MUST cite this requirement and
define which sources it contributes and when. The harness MUST include every
applicable contribution, deduplicate identical selections, and report
unresolvable mandatory inputs before inference. The complete set MUST be supplied
in the initial model request.
Generated output under project-root `evidence/`, including symlink aliases, MUST
be omitted from mandatory inputs when the default exclusion applies. An explicit
workspace allow MUST permit those selections; an explicit disallow MUST abort
under {cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial.mandatory`.
